headline: Strong El Nino -- RONI +1.69 degC (JAS 2026; legacy ONI +2.16), power index 83/100 (Very High), intensifying rapidly.
episode_status: El Nino conditions present for 4 consecutive seasons of RONI at or above +0.5 degC; 1 more needed before NOAA logs this as a formal episode.

mjo.note: CPC's newest pentad is 36 days old (25 Sep), too old to say where the active phase is now.

notes: 3 candidate analogs were dropped for being too dissimilar to the current trajectory.

alerts.title: Walker circulation response is extreme
alerts.detail: Composite atmospheric index +2.02 sigma across 10 independent feeds. Full coupling means the teleconnections are live, not merely possible.

alerts.title: Projected to peak in very strong territory
alerts.detail: Ensemble peak +2.28 degC at NDJ 2026, 81% probability of exceeding +2.0 degC.

alerts.title: RONI at or above +1.5 degC - Strong El Nino
alerts.detail: JAS 2026 RONI is +1.69 degC, which CPC prints as +1.7: Strong El Nino conditions this season. An event's category is set by its peak, which is still ahead of it while it is building.

alerts.title: Heat content still rising during an active event
alerts.detail: WWV is +0.052 x10^14 m3 per month and still climbing while the surface anomaly is already large. Events normally begin discharging by this stage; continued recharge means the event has not yet spent its fuel.

alerts.title: In-Fa: major typhoon, Category 3-equivalent typhoon
alerts.detail: 110 kt sustained, 953 mb, at 22.8N 143.5E in the West Pacific. It is over open ocean.

alerts.title: Third-warmest JAS or better
alerts.detail: Rank 2 of 77 for this calendar season on RONI.

alerts.title: Warm water volume in the top five on record
alerts.detail: Rank 3 of 561 months at +3.16 x10^14 m3.

alerts.title: El Nino conditions present, episode not yet formal
alerts.detail: El Nino conditions present for 4 consecutive seasons of RONI at or above +0.5 degC; 1 more needed before NOAA logs this as a formal episode.

alerts.title: Still intensifying
alerts.detail: RONI rose +0.33 degC from the previous season (intensifying rapidly).

alerts.title: Invest 91B: high potential for a tropical cyclone within 24 h
alerts.detail: JTWC's advisory of 31 Oct 2026 06:00 UTC places it near 9.7N 90.9E and rates the potential for a significant tropical cyclone within 24 hours high. A tropical cyclone formation alert is in effect until 2026-11-01 06:00 UTC: moving west-northwest at 14 kt, winds 28 to 33 kt, pressure near 998 mb.

alerts.title: East and central Pacific: 2.6x normal activity for the date
alerts.detail: 355 units of accumulated cyclone energy against 136 for a normal season by 31 October. 24 named storms, 13 hurricanes, 11 major.

alerts.title: Repeated westerly wind forcing over the warm pool
alerts.detail: 5 months in the last year averaged strongly westerly at 850 hPa in the western Pacific, which is how downwelling Kelvin waves get launched.

alerts.title: Legacy ONI and official RONI diverging
alerts.detail: ONI +2.16 against RONI +1.69, a gap of +0.47 degC. That much of the raw anomaly is the whole tropical ocean running warm rather than the Pacific, which is why CPC has classified on RONI since February 2026.

alerts.title: Atlantic: 0.17x normal activity for the date
alerts.detail: 20 units against 116 normal by 31 October. A suppressed basin is the expected signature of El Nino in the Atlantic, and it is not a reason to relax: 1992 was a quiet season and it produced Andrew.

alerts.title: Westerly wind event under way: east region, 180-150W, 5S-5N
alerts.detail: 29.5 days above +2 m/s since 2026-10-01 06Z in CCMP's near-real-time winds to 2026-10-30, peaking at +10.1 m/s on 2026-10-12. Equatorial westerly anomalies force downwelling Kelvin waves east.

outlook.label: Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands
outlook.text: 1. Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands: A broad area of low pressure is forecast to develop well to the southeast of the Hawaiian Islands by early next week. Thereafter, environmental conditions appear generally favorable for gradual development of this system, and a tropical depression could form by the end of next week as it moves westward to west-northwestward over the Central Pacific basin. Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent. Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

outlook.label: Invest 91B
outlook.text: THE AREA OF CONVECTION (INVEST 91B) PREVIOUSLY LOCATED NEAR 9.5N 93.2E IS NOW LOCATED NEAR 9.7N 90.9E, APPROXIMATELY 159 NM SOUTHWEST OF PORT BLAIR. ANIMATED MULTISPECTRAL SATELLITE IMAGE (MSI) AND A 302239Z SSMIS F18 91GHZ MICROWAVE IMAGE DEPICT A RAPIDLY CONSOLIDATING LLCC WITH DEEP, PERSISTENT CONVECTION BUILDING OVER THE CENTER OF THE LLCC. THE IMAGERY ALSO DEPICTS CURVED DEEP CONVECTIVE BANDING AND FORMATIVE RAIN BANDS FROM THE SOUTHERN QUADRANT TO THE NORTHERN QUADRANT. A PARTIAL 310331Z ASCAT-B PASS REVEALED AN EXTENSIVE FIELD OF 25-30KT WINDS ACROSS THE NORTHERN THROUGH SOUTHWESTERN SECTORS, WHILE A SMALL REGION OF 30-35KT WINDS WERE PRESENT IN THE SOUTHWESTERN QUADRANT OF THE LLCC. ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS REVEALS A FAVORABLE ENVIRONMENT FOR DEVELOPMENT WITH LOW TO MODERATE EASTERLY VERTICAL WIND SHEAR (VWS) OF 10-20KTS, GOOD UPPER- LEVEL WESTWARD AND POLEWARD OUTFLOW, AND WARM SEA SURFACE TEMPERATURES (SST) OF 29-30C. GLOBAL DETERMINISTIC AND ENSEMBLE MODELS ARE IN WEAK AGREEMENT ON THE FUTURE EVOLUTION OF 91B. THE GFS AND GEFS ENSEMBLES ARE PORTRAYING WEAK DEVELOPMENT, WHILE AND ECMWF AND ECEPS ARE PORTRAYING A MORE AGGRESSIVE DEVELOPMENT TIMELINE. THE OPERATIONAL GOOGLE DEEPMIND (GDM) ENSEMBLE IS ALSO AGGRESSIVE IN DEVELOPING 91B, INDICATING A 98 PERCENT PROBABILITY OF A TC WITHIN 12-18 HOURS. ALL MODELS ARE IN AGREEMENT IN 91B TRACKING NORTHWEST TOWARD MAINLAND INDIA OVER THE NEXT 24HRS. MAXIMUM SUSTAINED SURFACE WINDS ARE ESTIMATED AT 28 TO 33 KNOTS. MINIMUM SEA LEVEL PRESSURE IS ESTIMATED TO BE NEAR 1009 MB. THE POTENTIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A SIGNIFICANT TROPICAL CYCLONE WITHIN THE NEXT 24 HOURS IS UPGRADED TO HIGH. SEE REF A (WTIO21 PGTW 310600) FOR FURTHER DETAILS.

stormfury.verdict: 1 of 1 live storms fail STORMFURY's own criteria. Every one of them fails on supercooled water, which is the criterion no hurricane has ever passed and the reason the programme ended.
reasons: TRIGGER: the seeding agent needs supercooled liquid water and hurricane eyewalls are already glaciated at seeding altitude. Nothing to freeze, so the mechanism never starts. Willoughby et al., Bull. Am. Meteorol. Soc., 1985.

MAGNITUDE: across 37 natural eyewall expansions in 13 hurricanes this season, conserving angular momentum predicted a mean 28.0% wind drop and the storms actually gave up 4.3%, overstating it 6.5-fold. A hurricane is fed high-momentum air continuously, so a closed-system argument is an upper bound, not a forecast. STORMFURY's predicted effect came from that same calculation.

DETECTION: 25 of 322 unseeded hurricane intervals this season weakened by at least the 31% STORMFURY claimed for Debbie, and 59 moved that far in one direction or the other. An effect that size is indistinguishable from what hurricanes do untouched, which is what closed the programme.

programme.agencies: US Weather Bureau / NOAA with the US Navy

seeded_storms.name: Esther
seeded_storms.outcome: Flown before STORMFURY formally existed, as the proof of concept that got the programme funded.

seeded_storms.name: Beulah
seeded_storms.claimed: eyewall dissipated and reformed further out
seeded_storms.outcome: The first run missed the target area entirely. The second produced the reformation the hypothesis predicted, which is also what an unseeded eyewall replacement looks like.

seeded_storms.name: Debbie
seeded_storms.outcome: The showcase: five seedings on each of two days. These are the numbers the programme is remembered for, and the ones the natural replacement cycle later explained without any silver iodide.

seeded_storms.name: Ginger
seeded_storms.outcome: A large, diffuse storm with no coherent eyewall to move. It was seeded because it was what was available, which is itself a statement about how rarely the criteria above are met.

criteria.name: Within aircraft range
criteria.detail: 12,550 km from Lakeland, Florida, beyond the 2,040 km operational radius assumed here

criteria.name: Coherent eyewall
criteria.detail: 110 kt, but the deck reports no radius of maximum wind, so the eyewall's position is unknown

criteria.name: Clear of land for 24 h
criteria.detail: official track stays 1,027 km off the coast; no ensemble on file, so this is the deterministic track alone

criteria.name: Supercooled water to seed
criteria.detail: Hurricane eyewall updrafts are largely glaciated by the time they reach those temperatures. Warm-rain coalescence removes liquid water below the freezing level efficiently enough that little survives to be supercooled, leaving the seeding agent with nearly nothing to act on. The trigger is absent. The mechanism cannot start.

atlas.method: Past El Ninos (RONI >= +1.0) minus neutral years (|RONI| < 0.5), per season, per grid cell, since 1979, with each event and each neutral year counted once. Welch's t accompanies every difference and is judged against each season's own 95% point of Student's t. An event under way when the grids were built is left out.

cpc_discussion.synopsis: El Nino continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Nino likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance).
cpc_discussion.body:
El Nino strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Nino indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Nino-3.4, +3.0°C in Nino-3, and +3.9°C in Nino-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Nino.

The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Nino will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . Chances remain high for a historic event that would exceed the strength of previous El Nino events dating back to 1950 (+2.5°C or more for a 3-month RONI value ): the chance is 54% for September-November, 83% for October-December, and 70% for November-January. With an event of this magnitude, the chances of experiencing impacts consistent with El Nino are larger, though not guaranteed (see CPC outlooks for probabilities of seasonal anomalies). In summary, El Nino continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Nino likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance).
